rules.statement: Start every C# file with exactly the two lines `// Copyright © NCode Group` and `// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`, followed by a blank line, with no `#region` around them and no year.
rules.why: A header that nothing checks drifts from file to file. Leaving out the year means it never goes stale, and the SPDX identifier is the machine-readable form of the license that SPDX and REUSE tools read.
rules.check: Look for new or changed .cs files whose header is missing, has a different layout, includes a year or the full Apache boilerplate, or sits inside a #region. IDE0073 at warning with warnings-as-errors already fails the build on these.

rules.statement: Keep the `file_header_template` value in `.editorconfig` free of `;` and `#`, and don't make the Apache license boilerplate the template.
rules.why: Roslyn's `.editorconfig` parser ends a value at `;` or `#`. A value that contains either gets cut short, so IDE0073 never matches a file.
rules.check: Look at changes to `file_header_template` in .editorconfig and flag any value that contains `;` or `#`, such as the Apache notice's `(the "License");`.

rules.statement: Don't report a missing or different file header on generated code, such as EF Core migrations marked `generated_code = true` or a file that starts with `// <auto-generated`.
rules.why: Generated code is exempt from the header rule, and the analyzer skips these files.
rules.check: Before reporting a header problem, check whether the file starts with `// <auto-generated` or is covered by a `generated_code = true` section in .editorconfig.

rules.statement: Keep the file-header text in the Rider `.DotSettings` file identical to the `.editorconfig` `file_header_template`.
rules.why: Then Rider's code cleanup writes the same header that Visual Studio and the IDE0073 fix write.
rules.check: When either the `.DotSettings` header text or `file_header_template` changes, check that the other one changes to match.

rules.statement: Put a repository's own `[*.cs]` override of `file_header_template` and the `IDE0073` severity after the shared template's `[*.cs]` section in `.editorconfig`, and set IDE0073 to `warning` there.
rules.why: The later section wins for both keys, so the header stays the repository's decision even if the template's section changes. At `warning`, warnings-as-errors makes a bad header fail the build.
rules.check: In .editorconfig changes, check that the repository's header settings come after the template's section and that `dotnet_diagnostic.IDE0073.severity` is `warning`, not `suggestion`.
